meta.description: The machine-checkable subset of voice.md. Kept deliberately small and high precision: a check that cries wolf gets ignored, which is worse than no check. Disable a rule by setting enabled to false rather than by learning to skip its output.
meta.note: Patterns are Python regex, matched case-insensitively unless case_sensitive is true. Fenced code blocks and inline code are excluded before matching.

rules.why: The single most reliable tell of unedited AI output.
rules.message: em-dash or en-dash. Use a period, comma, colon, parentheses, or restructure.

rules.why: The most overused construction in AI-written copy, and instantly recognisable.
rules.message: staccato fragment framing. Write it as a normal sentence.

rules.why: Phrases that appear almost exclusively in machine-written prose.
patterns: (^|[.!?]\s+)at the end of the day\b|at the end of the day,

rules.why: Adjectives that assert value instead of demonstrating it.
rules.message: marketing fluff. Show the thing instead of asserting it.

rules.why: Pre-empting a misreading the reader was never going to have. One deliberate antithesis is fine, the habit is not.
rules.message: possible over-clarifying. State the thing and trust the reader.

rules.why: Announcing what the page contains, instead of getting on with it. Reads as a table of contents in prose and is a standard content-mill opener. Flagged by Aditya on a real draft: 'Here is what to look for, five options compared honestly, and who each one suits' should have been 'an honest comparison of the top planners, and what to look for'.
patterns: here('s| is| are) what (you'll|you will|we'll|we will|to)\b
rules.message: announces the contents instead of delivering them. Lead with the thing.

rules.why: Softening every claim reads as having nothing to say.
rules.message: hedging. Say it or cut it.

rules.why: Bullets are easier for a model to generate than a paragraph that holds together, so unedited drafts over-list.
rules.message: more than 40 percent of lines are bullets. Turn the argument back into prose.
